overview.description: All Fours is a classic trump trick-taking game defined by four scoring elements: High, Low, Jack, and Game. This base profile follows the Trinidad structure, with related English and North American forms listed as variations.

history.origins: All Fours emerged in England in the 17th century and later spread to North America and the Caribbean.
timeline: 1674: Charles Cotton records an early two-player form.
19th century: North American Old Sledge / Seven Up forms become common.
20th-21st century: Trinidad partnership form becomes the best-known living version, while Yorkshire and Lancashire forms continue in England.
history.evolution: Many descendants branch from the same High-Low-Jack-Game core: Pitch, Pedro, and regional All Fours family games.
history.cultural: All Fours is considered a heritage game in Trinidad and Tobago and remains a pub/league game in parts of northern England.

setup.players: 2-4 players; with 4, fixed partnerships across the table.
setup.dealing: Deal six cards to each player, then turn one card up for provisional trumps.

rules.objective: Reach the target score by collecting High, Low, Jack, and Game points each hand.
rules.gameplay: After six cards each and a turned trump indicator, eldest hand may stand or beg. If begging is accepted, dealer runs three more cards each and turns again until trump suit changes. In play, highest trump wins a trick; if no trump is played, highest card of the led suit wins. Players with the led suit may either follow suit or play trump, but cannot throw a non-trump card of another suit when they could follow. Score hand points in order High, Low, Jack, Game; first side to target wins the game.
keyRules: High: point to side originally holding highest trump dealt.
Low: point to side originally holding lowest trump dealt.
Jack: point if your side wins trick containing jack of trumps (hang-jack variants award extra on capture).
Game: point to side with higher trick-card value total (A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1, 10=10).
Scores are pegged in fixed order High, Low, Jack, Game to resolve close finishes.

strategy.basic: Secure High and Low early by controlling trump suit length and timing.
strategy.intermediate: Protect or attack the Jack of trumps; that point often decides hands near the finish.
strategy.advanced: Track tens and honors in captured tricks to manage the Game point race even when trump control is split.
tips: Do not spend top trump too early if Jack is still unseen.
Game point math is ten-heavy; saving tens in winning tricks is critical.

list.name: Trinidad All Fours
list.description: Anticlockwise play, beg/take-one flow, target commonly 14, with hang-jack convention in many tables.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Trinidad partnership rules align with this base profile; no separate engine overrides have been modeled yet.

list.name: West Yorkshire All Fours
list.description: Pitch-led trump (no turn-up), scoring target 11, and regional partnership signaling/throw-in conventions.
list.emptyOverridesReason: West Yorkshire league rules are documented in sources, but detailed engine overrides are not yet encoded for this profile.

list.name: Lancashire All Fours
list.description: Related to Yorkshire form, but Low can be awarded to trick winner of the low trump.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Lancashire differences are summarized in text; engine-level changes such as Low handling are not yet split into overrides.

list.name: North American Seven Up / Old Sledge
list.description: Clockwise forms with gift/run options, often to 7 or 10, and tie conventions for Game point.
list.emptyOverridesReason: North American Seven Up uses the same High-Low-Jack-Game core; scoring and target variations are noted but not yet parameterized.

list.name: 17th-Century All Fours
list.description: Two-player historical form from Cotton with related run-card and scoring details.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Cotton’s historical rules are captured in history text; this engine does not yet branch into a dedicated 17th-century override.

phases.label: Deal
phases.notes: Deal six cards to each player.

phases.label: Turn Trump Card
phases.notes: Turn next stock card to propose trump suit.

phases.label: Eldest Decision
phases.notes: Player on dealer's right stands or begs.

phases.label: Take One or Run Cards
phases.notes: Dealer either gives one point to opponents or runs cards (3 each + new turn-up) until suit changes.

phases.label: Trick Play
phases.notes: Highest trump wins trick; if no trump, highest led suit wins.

phases.label: Score High Low Jack Game
phases.notes: Apply score order High, Low, Jack, Game and check target.

ante.reason: All Fours uses Beg/Stand and point scoring; no ante.

deal.description: Dealer distributes initial cards and run-cards packets.
deal.constraints: Dealer only during deal and dealer-response phases.

reveal_market.description: Turn up card to indicate current trump suit.
reveal_market.constraints: Dealer only after deal or run-cards packet.

buy_market.reason: Trump is set by turn-up and Beg/Stand; no market purchase.

buy_stock.reason: Six cards dealt; no draw from stock during play.

fold.reason: Trick-taking; all must play each trick. No fold.

check.description: Dealer accepts current trump and gives one point to begging side (take one).

call.reason: Points for High, Low, Jack, Game; no betting call.

bet.reason: Scoring is by card points, not bets.

raise.reason: No betting rounds in All Fours.

declare.reason: Points awarded at hand end; no declare phase.

reveal_hand.reason: Cards played to tricks; no showdown reveal.

award_pot.description: Award scoring points for High, Low, Jack, and Game.

play_card.description: Play one card to current trick.
play_card.constraints: Must follow led suit or play trump if possible; cannot discard off-suit non-trump when holding led suit.

draw.reason: Six cards dealt; no draw during trick play.

discard.reason: Cards are played to tricks, not to a discard pile.

pass.description: Stand on current turned trump suit.
pass.constraints: Used by eldest hand in beg-or-stand phase.

bid.constraints: Used by eldest hand in beg-or-stand phase.

meld.reason: Trick-taking; no melds. Points are High, Low, Jack, Game.

go_out.reason: Hand ends when all tricks are played; no go-out declaration.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: On non-trump leads, a player who holds led suit may either follow suit or play trump.

edgeCases.text: If dealer runs cards and the new turn-up suit matches the previous one, deal three more each and turn again until suit changes.
Low point belongs to original holder of the lowest trump dealt, not necessarily trick winner.
Off-suit non-trump play while able to follow suit is a revoke and must trigger penalty handling per chosen variant.

engine.rankingSystem: All Fours scoring (High, Low, Jack, Game)
engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. Trump is set by the turn-up card and by beg or run rules; no jokers.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). The trump suit is set by the turn-up and by beg or run flow; it outranks plain suits when winning tricks and for scoring High, Low, Jack, and Game.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit in order ace, king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two. Trump overrides plain suit in trick resolution; jack of trump is often the right bower.
engine.dealPattern: Deal 6 each, turn trump, optional beg/run-cards cycle, then play all tricks.

synthesis.shortDescription: Classic trump trick-taking game where every hand awards High, Low, Jack, and Game.

prompts.human: All Fours: six cards each, trump turned up, then eldest hand can stand or beg for new trumps. Win tricks to score High, Low, Jack, and Game; points are pegged in that order.
prompts.ai: Game: All Fours (Trinidad base). Flow: deal six, reveal trump, stand-or-beg, dealer take-one or run-cards, trick play, score High/Low/Jack/Game in strict order. Enforce follow-or-trump rule on non-trump leads.

scoring.description: Each hand can award up to four core points: High, Low, Jack, and Game.
scoring.winCondition: First side to 14 points in this base profile wins; other targets are variation-specific.

penalties.Revoke: Playing an illegal off-suit non-trump when able to follow can incur point or hand penalties depending on table variant.
